FN-SLIJC88-1
FISCAL NOTE
House Bill 4
Committee: Ways and Means Education Sponsor: Senator Matt Woods
Analyst: Jennifer Farish Date: 02/03/2026
House Bill 4 as introduced would decrease potential receipts to the Education Trust Fund by an
estimated $7.2 million annually for fiscal years 2027 through 2029 by exempting the purchase
of certain broadband equipment and supplies from projects funded or administered by the
Alabama Department of Economic and Community Affairs (ADECA) from state sales and use
tax for that time period.
Further, this bill could also decrease sales and use tax receipts to local governments by a
cumulative estimated maximum amount of $9.45 million annually, if all local governments
adopted the exemption provided by this bill.
ADECA's Alabama Connectivity Plan report from 2021 estimated the total cost to provide
certain statewide fiber connectivity at $4.5 billion over a 10-year period. ADECA attributed an
estimated 40% of project costs ($1.8 billion) to material.
